To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the native state of a protein can be identified among low-resolution structural models by explicit solvent microsecond molecular dynamics simulations using the latest-generation of protein force fields.
the native state can be identified among the non-native ensembles of a protein by the free energy and the von Mises estimator of entropy in dihedral angles.

explicit solvent micro-second MD simulations using the CHARMM36 force field are sufficiently accurate to identify the native structure among low-resolution structural models, and that the von Mises distribution is a useful tool for the analysis of the dihedral angle distribution in MD simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of all-atom molecular dynamic simulations in explicit solvent in combination with free energy calculations to identify native states from non-native ensembles.
the application of all-atom explicit solvent MD simulations in the context of protein structure determination.

the development of new methods to improve protein structure predictions and the refinement of experimental structures, and to provide a better understanding of the dynamic and thermodynamic properties of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MD simulations of ∝ 1 μs are sufficient to identify the native state among non-native encales, provided that the force field and free energy metrics have been carefully calibrated.
the MD method is a powerful tool for the refinement of protein structures and for the determination of native-like ensembles.
the native structure can only be identified among nonnative ensembles if a free energy and an entropic metric are used together.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MD simulations are capable of improving protein structures, especially for those with large conformational changes.
the native state of proteins can be accurately identified by microsecond MD simulation using the latest generation force fields and free energies.
the native-like ensembles are those which are most stable, i.e., those with the lowest free energy and longest residence times.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the free energy landscape of protein folding is sufficiently rugged that it is possible to find a native-like ensemble among non-native conformations, and that this ensemble can be identified by a combination of the free energy and the von Mises entropic estimator.
the native state of a protein is not only the most stable state, but also the state with the highest entropy.
MD simulation of protein structures can be used to assess their quality and to identify native-like conformations.
